pk.context: 40 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: An antisecretory effect lasting longer than 24 hours, despite a one-hour half-life, sets this proton pump inhibitor apart.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 77%, and food does not alter the peak level or extent of absorption. About 98% is bound to protein, and about 71% of a dose is excreted in urine after hepatic metabolism.
A sodium salt in sesquihydrate form, with a molecular weight of 383.4 for the active moiety. It is a crystalline powder that is racemic and freely soluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 20 mg and 40 mg delayed-release tablets, plus a 40 mg packet of granules for oral suspension.

Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or its chemical relatives and with rilpivirine-containing products, with no boxed warning. Headache and diarrhea are the most frequent adverse reactions.
Short-term treatment and maintenance of healing in erosive esophagitis associated with reflux disease, and pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Covalently binds the (H+,K+)-ATPase of gastric parietal cells, inhibiting both basal and stimulated acid secretion for more than 24 hours.
The generic name begins with P and has twelve letters.
